name: Capillary Malformation-Arteriovenous Malformation Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of multiple small, round to oval capillary malformations often with a pale halo
Identification of high-flow arteriovenous malformations or fistulas by imaging
Detection of pathogenic mutation in RASA1 gene
Family history of similar vascular anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple capillary malformations plus at least one high-flow arteriovenous malformation or fistula
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for RASA1 mutations supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple small capillary malformations with pale halo

common.symptomName: Localized pain or swelling over AVMs
Warmth and pulsation over vascular malformations

occasional.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to cerebral AVMs
High-output cardiac failure secondary to large AVMs
Ulceration or skin breakdown over malformations
Limb hypertrophy associated with vascular anomalies

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing pathogenic RASA1 mutations
imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing high-flow vascular lesions
Conventional angiography confirming AVMs or fistulas
other: Family history of similar vascular anomalies
Physical exam revealing multiple capillary malformations with pale halos

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of multiple capillary malformations with pale halo
Facial port-wine stain in trigeminal nerve distribution

references: Eerola I, Boon LM, Mulliken JB, et al. Capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation, a new clinical and genetic disorder caused by RASA1 mutations. Am J Hum Genet. 2003;73(6):1240-1249.
Revencu N, Boon LM, Mendola A, et al. RASA1 mutations and associated phenotypes in capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation syndrome. Hum Mutat. 2008;29(4):E283-E291.
